## Mini Lisp: s-expressions with integers, strings and symbols. The
## atom alternation is ordered number / string / symbol — same-length
## shapes, so the order only expresses intent, and the recursion stays
## sexp -> list -> sexp.
grammar MiniLisp version "1.0.0" edition "v1" {
  ws = %x20 / %x09 / %x0A
  pq = *ws
  digit = %x30-39
  number = [ %x2D ] 1*digit as number
  schar = %x01-21 / %x23-5B / %x5D-10FFFF
  string = %x22 *schar %x22 as string
  ## printable minus space, parens, quote and semicolon.
  ychar = %x21 / %x23-27 / %x2A-5B / %x5D-7E
  symbol = 1*ychar as symbol
  atom = number / string / symbol
  list = "(" pq *( sexp pq ) ")" as forms
  sexp = atom / list
  top = pq sexp pq

  entry main: top

  test {
    accept "42"
    accept "(define x 1)"
    accept "(+ 1 (* 2 3))"
    accept "(print \"hello\" (list a b))"
    accept "(neg -5)"
    reject "(unclosed"
    reject "\"unterminated"
    accept "()"   # the empty list is a value
  }
}
